title: Add a container element to render progress steps / timeline / chain of thought
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary Add a new container element that can be used to show a list of events in chronological order. This is a common UI pattern to display AI reasoning steps. ### Why? _No response_ ### How? This element needs to allow step-by-step progress, so we need to use a pattern that is closer to `st.status` and not require declaring everything from the beginning, as with `st.tabs`: ```python with st.progress_steps() as steps: with steps.add_step("Searching for profiles", icon=":material/search"): st.markdown("Found the profile.") with steps.add_step("Found profile picture' , icon=":material/profile"): st.image(profile_url) ``` Alternative names: `st.timeline`, `st.chain_of_thought`, `st.feeds`, `st.status_steps`, `st.steps` It might be nice to make each step collapsible, similar to how we do it in the navigation menu. ### Additional Context - Might be slightly related to #10748 - https://eui.elastic.co/docs/components/display/timeline/ - https://chakra-ui.com/docs/components/timeline - https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/lists/feeds - https://baseweb.design/components/progress-steps/ - https://ai-sdk.dev/elements/components/chain-of-thought

## Update

Streamlit 1.63 will provide a `type="step"` for `st.expander` and `st.status` that allows to create progress steps, timelines and chain of thought UI, for example:

```python
with st.chat_message("assistant"):
    with st.status(":shimmer[Thinking]", type="compact") as status:
        with st.status("Searching docs", type="step"):
            sources = search(prompt)
            st.write(sources[0])

        with st.status("Planning", type="step"):
            st.write(reasoning)

        status.update(label="Thought for 4 seconds", state="complete")

    response = st.write_stream(get_streaming_response(prompt, sources))
```
